params.body:
Fixes bevinding een-zwijgende-partner-neemt-de-pagina-mee. Nightwatch #34, and #21 with it.

`WebsiteController::index` asks `RealGarantService::isConnected()`, and that is a real login at
RealGarant. The seal rule at the top of `isConnected` covers an environment that may **not** call
out; it does not cover one that may and gets no answer. The `ConnectionException` then came straight
up and the **public stock list on a dealer's own website** answered 500.

22 September 2026 at 01:08: `cURL error 28: Operation timed out after 10002 milliseconds` on
`rg-wms.com/rest/auth`, and the request came from **Googlebot**. So ten seconds of silence at a third
party decided whether our customer's site worked, and what Google saw of it.

The exception is caught where the answer is read. No token means "not connected", the warranty UI
disappears and the page renders, which is exactly what the comment above `isConnected` already
promised for the sealed case.

The failure is remembered for a minute, like a refused login one line below. Without that every page
view pays the full ten-second timeout again, and a slow partner becomes a slow site for everyone.
The second test pins that: two calls, one attempt.

Both tests fail against the service on main, with the ConnectionException escaping.

#21 (`cURL error 52: Empty reply from server`, 21 September, same host) is the same family and is
covered by the same catch.
params.title: A silent partner does not take the public page with it
